title: The Robber Bishop
translation: Near Yanagihara there lived a priest everyone called the Robber Bishop. Apparently he'd been robbed so many times that people started calling him that.
original: {柳原|やなぎはら}の{辺|ほとり}に、{強盗|がうだう}{法印|ほふいん}と{号|がう}する{僧|そう}ありけり。
{度々|たびたび}{強盗|がうだう}にあひたる{故|ゆゑ}に、この{名|な}をつけにけるとぞ。
literal: Around Yanagihara there was a priest called the Robber Hōin.
It is said that, because he had met with robbers many times, he was given this name.

notes.text: Yanagihara: an area of Kyoto, probably in the north-east of the city. The exact place is not certain.
{強盗|がうだう}: 'robber, armed robbery'. Modern ごうとう. {法印|ほふいん}: the highest honorary rank for priests, so the translation says 'bishop' (compare section 45). The name sounds like he is the robber.
{号|がう}す: 'to be called, to go by the name'.

notes.quote: この名をつけにけるとぞ
notes.text: とぞ: 'so they say'. The verb (いふ, 'they say') is left out, a common way to end a story heard from others. The whole section is two sentences long: the name, and the explanation.
